name: pysubs2
role: Python library and CLI to edit, retime and convert subtitle files, writing ASS styles from code
summary: Python library and `pysubs2` CLI for SRT, ASS/SSA, WebVTT, MicroDVD, MPL2, TMP, JSON and TTML. It writes ASS styles and override-tag events from code, retimes in milliseconds and converts between formats; it does not render.
use_when: Write ASS styles and events from code as input for libass or FFmpeg burned-in captions
Retime or convert subtitle files in a script; over ttconv when ASS styling matters
avoid_when: Delivery formats such as IMSC, SCC or EBU STL: ttconv

install.macos: python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install pysubs2==1.9.1

notes: 2026-11-27: the CLI's -o takes an output directory, not a file; without it files are rewritten in place. ASS times are written as centiseconds.

assessment.rationale: PyPI 1.9.1 uploaded 2026-10-30 (Python >=3.12), repository pushed 2026-11-10; MIT per installed metadata, no dependencies. Nothing catalogued writes ASS styles and events from code: libass renders but does not edit, ttconv skips ASS styling, caption-checker only checks.

evidence.result: 11 checks pass, repeat processes identical: ASS built from code (Kinetic style, \an8 \fad \k tags) reloads with tags and ms timings; SRT to ASS with +2.5 s shift gives 3 cues at 3500-5000, 5620-7540, 8000-9750 ms; CLI SRT to WebVTT leaves input unchanged. Python 3.12.2.
evidence.scope: ASS authoring, SRT to ASS shift and CLI to WebVTT as text; not libass rendering, frame-rate transforms, other formats or encodings; macOS arm64, Python 3.12.
